analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7176, its 6th straight decline and longest losing streak since April 2024. A 7th down day would be the longest run since February 2020.

Breadth was the weakest of 2026: 464 S&P 500 decliners (most since Dec 31), all 24 sector groups fell, and the equal-weight index fell 1.77%. Defensives dropped too (Staples -1.48%, Health Care -2.07%).
The S&P 500 is down 5.10% for the week, on track for its worst week since the April 2025 Liberation Day tariffs. The VIX rose 3.88 points to 28.44, its highest since March.
Tech declines were similar in size: Nasdaq -2.25%, Magnificent 7 -2.67%, Philly semiconductor index -2.41%.
Asia is extending the selloff this morning, led by chipmakers: TAIEX -6.23% (7-month low), KOSPI -5.44% (9-month low), Nikkei -4.92%, Hang Seng -2.33% (nearly 20% below its January peak).
Futures are lower this morning: S&P 500 -0.50%, Nasdaq 100 -0.98%, Stoxx -1.70%.
Gold fell 2.68% to a 14-month low of $3,625/oz and is down another 2.2% this morning. Bitcoin fell 1.25% to its lowest since early July. US HY spreads widened 6bps to 344bps, the widest since May.

Energy prices rose on Iran headlines (Axios: White House asked the Pentagon how Iran would respond to strike scenarios; NYT: Trump considering further strikes). European gas futures rose 4.46% to €84.46/MWh. Oil settled little changed on demand concerns.
Putin promised forceful retaliation after Ukraine damaged the Crimea bridge and said the strike ended talk of a partial ceasefire.

European sovereign yields rose on higher near-term inflation expectations: Bund 10yr +3.5bps to 3.40%, OAT +6.8bps, gilt +2.6bps. The 1yr Euro inflation swap rose 1.1bps to 3.01%, and ECB hikes priced by Sep 2027 rose 3.1bps to 69bps.
Bundesbank's Nagel said the ECB may need to tighten further, but sees lower second-round effect risk than in 2022 and no wage-price spiral.
US 10yr yield fell 2.3bps to 5.05% (about 5.01% this morning) and the 2yr fell 4.2bps to 4.76% as equities sold off. Initial jobless claims rose to 203k vs 198k expected.

Fed speakers stayed hawkish. Goolsbee cited 'multiple months in a row of borderline disturbingly high inflation' and will consider all options in December. Barr sees further rate adjustments ahead and called financial conditions 'quite accommodative'.
Japan October core CPI was 2.2% YoY vs 2.3% consensus. Headline CPI rose to 2.3%. DB says this is unlikely to alter the BOJ's path or a December hike.
Trump, Xi and Putin announced plans to boost refined petroleum product supply. DB sees the supply impact as uncertain given constraints, including Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries.
